in	springtime	no	less	marvellous	than	in	high	summer.
At	 last	 they	 came	 up	 the	 long	 road,	 and	 reached	 the
very	 pass	 where	 the	 goblins	 had	 captured	 them	 before.
But	they	came	to	that	high	point	at	morning,	and	looking
backward	 they	 saw	 a	 white	 sun	 shining	 over	 the
outstretched	 lands.	 There	 behind	 lay	 Mirkwood,	 blue	 in
the	distance,	and	darkly	green	at	the	nearer	edge	even	in
the	spring.	There	far	away	was	the	Lonely	Mountain	on
the	 edge	 of	 eyesight.	 On	 its	 highest	 peak	 snow	 yet
unmelted	was	gleaming	pale.
“So	comes	snow	after	fire,	and	even	dragons	have	their
ending!”	 said	 Bilbo,	 and	 he	 turned	 his	 back	 on	 his
adventure.	 The	 Tookish	 part	 was	 getting	 very	 tired,	 and
the	Baggins	was	daily	getting	stronger.	“I	wish	now	only
to	be	in	my	own	armchair!”	he	said.
